body:
[P1] `tests/behavioral/test_language.py:45` — Harness "Spanish intake" / catalog-form tests script the already-correct reply, so they cannot fail if the agent again leaks English training vocab.

`test_spanish_intake_goal_question_uses_spanish_vocabulary` uses `steps=[message(CORRECTED)]`; `ConversationHarness.say` enqueues that on `ScriptedModel` and returns the canned text as `reply`. `find_english_leaks` only sees `CORRECTED`. Same tautology in `test_catalog_names_stay_in_catalog_form_in_spanish_chat` (line 55): the ideal reply including `bench press` is hardcoded.

Failure: prompt regresses and the live agent again replies with "muscle" during Spanish intake (or translates catalog lifts / leaks "strength"); CI stays green because the scripted model cannot produce a failing reply. The pure unit tests on `OBSERVED_LEAK`/`CORRECTED` and the instructions pin are real, but these harness tests add no agent-behavior signal — same #51 lesson as `tests/test_agent_tone.py`.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:33` — Multi-word lexicon entries are compiled as exact single-space phrases, so common variants of "weight loss" are not detected.

Multi-word terms use `rf"\b{re.escape(term)}\b"`, so `"weight loss"` becomes `\bweight\ loss\b` and matches only a single literal space. `weight-loss`, `weight  loss`, `weight\nloss`, and `weight\tloss` all return empty from `find_english_leaks`. Unlike "fat loss", there is no standalone "weight" lexicon entry, so those variants have no single-word fallback. The offline CI gate can treat a real English leak of a listed phrase as clean.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:36` — Lexicon uses bare `\b` word boundaries, so terms like "muscle"/"strength" also match inside multi-word or hyphenated exercise names the carve-out must allow.

`_compile` builds `r"\b" + parts + r"\b"`, and in Python `\b` treats `-` as a non-word character, so there is a boundary between the letters and the hyphen.

Reproduced:
- `find_english_leaks("Muscle-up")` → `{"muscle"}`
- `find_english_leaks("muscle up")` → `{"muscle"}`
- `find_english_leaks("Hoy hicimos Muscle-up y dips")` → `{"muscle"}`
- `find_english_leaks("strength band pull-apart")` → `{"strength"}`

A Spanish reply that correctly keeps a hyphenated/multi-word catalog lift containing a lexicon token is flagged as a leak. The seed collision pin only checks current `SEED_EXERCISES` (no muscle-up today), so it does not protect growing catalog names or compounds. Multi-word lexicon entries correctly allow `[\s-]+` between their own parts, but single-token terms still use bare `\b` and match inside hyphenated names.

- pi code-review

[P1] `tests/behavioral/language.py:70` — Compound spans expand unbounded across every single-space non-connector neighbor, so ordinary Spanish content words absorb nearby lexicon hits and suppress real leaks.

The left/right while-loops in `_compound_spans` extend a hyphenated token over every single-space neighbor that is not in `_CONNECTORS` and not itself hyphenated, with no bound. Words like `hacer`, `hoy`, `ganar`, `haz`, `es`, `muscle`, `strength` are not connectors, so they get swallowed into the compound span and then suppressed by `_inside_a_compound`.

Reproduced:
- `find_english_leaks('vamos a hacer muscle pull-ups hoy')` → `set()` (should be `{'muscle'}`)
- `find_english_leaks('para ganar strength haz Muscle-up')` → `set()` (should be `{'strength'}`)
- `find_english_leaks('tu muscle es weight-loss')` → `{'weight loss'}` only — misses `muscle`
- `find_english_leaks('haz pull-ups strength por favor')` → `set()`

Connector breaks still work (`ganar muscle y hacer pull-ups` flags `muscle`), so the intended narrow exemption over-broadened into a leak hide.

- pi code-review

[P1] `tests/behavioral/language.py:96` — Hyphen-span non-exemption only keeps hits that fully cover the hyphenated token, so multi-word (or partial) lexicon matches inside longer compounds are dropped as "in-name".

`_inside_a_compound` suppresses a hit when it sits inside a compound unless `hit` fully covers the hyphenated token (`hit[0] <= h_start and hit[1] >= h_end`). Any match that only partially overlaps a longer hyphenated token is treated as exercise-name geometry and silenced.

Reproduced:
- `find_english_leaks('weight-loss-plan')` → `set()` (should flag `weight loss`)
- `find_english_leaks('pre-weight-loss')` → `set()`
- `find_english_leaks('fat loss-goal')` / `'weight loss-plan'` → `set()`
- `find_english_leaks('muscle-building')` / `'strength-focus'` / `'lean-mass'` → `set()`

Only the exact token `weight-loss` still flags. Real training-vocab leaks in compound form green-pass the offline CI gate while violating the Agent rule (catalog names only). Prefer hyphen-aware term boundaries (or limit the exemption to "hit is a proper substring of one hyphenated token") over unbounded multi-token shape walking.

- pi code-review

[P1] `tests/behavioral/language.py:80` — Exercise-name span extension is still unbounded over any non-Spanish neighbor, so lexicon leaks adjacent to a real particle compound are absorbed into the exemption.

`_exercise_name_spans` left/right-extends a particle hyphen core over every single-space neighbor not in the tiny `_SPANISH_WORDS` set, with no bound. Round-3 special-cased plural `pull-ups` (not a core) and added `haz`, but the absorb loops are unchanged for actual particle cores (`pull-up`, `Muscle-up`, `pull-apart`).

Reproduced:
- `find_english_leaks('haz pull-up strength por favor')` → `set()` (should flag `strength`)
- `find_english_leaks('pull-up for strength')` → `set()`
- `find_english_leaks('strength Muscle-up')` / `('Muscle-up strength')` / `('muscle pull-apart')` → `set()`
- `find_english_leaks('vamos a hacer strength Muscle-up hoy')` → `set()` (`hacer`/`hoy` are not breakers)
- `find_english_leaks('Hoy toca strength band pull-apart')` → `set()` (whole string one span)

Contrast: `strength haz Muscle-up` and `muscle pull-ups` correctly flag. Bound absorption (e.g. core token only, or at most known English modifiers like `band`) so space-separated goal vocab next to a compound still leaks.

- pi code-review

[P1] `tests/behavioral/language.py:77` — Any hyphenated token that merely contains a direction particle becomes an exercise core, including lexicon+particle phrases that are not exercise names.

`_exercise_name_spans` treats any hyphenated token whose parts include a `_PARTICLES` member (`up`/`down`/`apart`/`over`/`out`/`through`) as a name core, and `find_english_leaks` drops any lexicon hit fully inside those spans.

Reproduced false negatives:
- `find_english_leaks('lean-out')` → `set()` (should flag `lean`)
- `find_english_leaks('cutting-down')` → `set()` (should flag `cutting`)
- `find_english_leaks('bulking-up')` / `('muscles-up')` / `('fat-over')` → `set()`
- `find_english_leaks('strength-through-progress')` → `set()` (should flag `strength`)

Legitimate names (`Muscle-up`, `strength band pull-apart`) are correctly exempted, but particle-in-token is over-broad. Require a non-lexicon movement head (or an allowlist of known name shapes), not “any token that contains `up`/`out`/…”.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:53` — Particles are singular-only, so legitimate plural exercise shapes whose head is a lexicon word false-positive as leaks.

`_PARTICLES` is deliberately singular (`up` not `ups`) so `muscle pull-ups` still flags. That also means `Muscle-ups` has parts `['Muscle','ups']`, builds no span, and `\bmuscle\b` matches the head.

Reproduced:
- `find_english_leaks('Muscle-up')` → `set()`
- `find_english_leaks('Muscle-ups')` / `('muscle-ups')` → `{'muscle'}`
- `find_english_leaks('strength band pull-aparts')` → `{'strength'}`
- `find_english_leaks('Hoy toca muscle-ups y dips')` → `{'muscle'}`

A Spanish reply that correctly keeps a plural catalog-style name fails the offline CI gate. Accept optional trailing `s` on particles (`ups`/`downs`/…) for the core token only, without treating space-separated `pull-ups` as a multi-token compound core.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:73` — `_is_name_core` only accepts exact allowlist equality (or a trailing `s`), so hyphen-joined extensions of an allowlisted core are not name spans.

`_TOKEN_RE` keeps hyphenated forms as one token. Equipment absorption only walks **space-separated** previous tokens, so it never peels prefixes inside a single hyphenated token. Lexicon `\b` still matches heads at hyphens.

Reproduced:
- `find_english_leaks('bar-muscle-up')` / `ring-muscle-up` / `kipping-muscle-up` → `{'muscle'}`
- `find_english_leaks('strength-band-pull-apart')` → `{'strength'}`
- Contrast space-separated twins: `bar muscle-up`, `strength band pull-apart` → clean

A Spanish reply that keeps a legitimate compound written as one hyphenated token fails CI while the spaced form passes. Either treat an allowlisted core as a hyphen **suffix** of the token (`*-muscle-up`, `*-pull-apart`), or normalize/split equipment prefixes inside hyphenated tokens the same way the space walk does.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:70` — `_EQUIPMENT_MODIFIERS` is singular-only, so plural equipment bridges break the `strength` prefix rule.

Cores explicitly allow a trailing `s` (`muscle-ups`, `pull-aparts`), but equipment is only `band`/`bar`/`ring`/`cable`. `strength` is absorbed only when `following in _EQUIPMENT_MODIFIERS`.

Reproduced:
- `find_english_leaks('strength band pull-apart')` → clean
- `find_english_leaks('strength bands pull-apart')` → `{'strength'}`
- Same for `strength rings muscle-up`, `strength bars pull-over`, `strength cables pull-through`

Singular form is green; plural equipment surface flags a real goal-vocab false positive next to a legitimate compound. Accept optional trailing `s` on equipment modifiers (or strip a final `s` before the set check), matching how cores handle plurals.

- pi code-review

[P1] `tests/behavioral/language.py:80` — Hyphen-suffix name-core check accepts any prefix, so lexicon terms glued onto a core are carved out as exercise names.

Round-5 `_is_name_core` returns true for any token that `endswith(f"-{core}")` (optional trailing `s`). `_TOKEN_RE` keeps the whole hyphen chain as one token, and `_exercise_name_spans` exempts that entire span — so lexicon hits inside the prefix never flag.

Reproduced:
- `find_english_leaks('muscle-pull-up')` / `strength-pull-up` / `fat-pull-up` / `lean-muscle-up` / `cutting-pull-up` → `set()`
- `find_english_leaks('weight-loss-pull-up')` / `fat-loss-muscle-up` / `muscle-building-pull-up` → `set()`
- Contrast space-separated near-core leaks still flag: `muscle pull-up`, `strength pull-up`, `strength Muscle-up` → `{muscle}`/`{strength}`
- Intended names still clean: `bar-muscle-up`, `kipping-muscle-up`, `strength-band-pull-apart`

Same dual policy shows up as separator-dependent outcomes: `strength-muscle-up` clean vs `strength Muscle-up` flags; `strength-band-pull-apart` clean vs `strength-band pull-apart` flags.

Restrict hyphen prefixes to a real equipment/variant allowlist (or peel only known prefixes), matching the space-path `_EQUIPMENT_MODIFIERS` + `strength`-before-equipment rule — not unbounded `endswith(-{core})`.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:126` — Space-path strength absorption only accepts a *bare* following equipment token, so mixed space/hyphen name shapes false-positive `{strength}` while fully spaced and fully hyphenated twins stay clean.

`_is_name_core` accepts equipment-prefixed hyphen cores (`band-pull-apart`, `bar-muscle-up`), but the left-absorb loop only checks:

```python
_equipment_base(following) in _EQUIPMENT_MODIFIERS  # whole next token
# or word == "strength" and following is bare equipment
```

It never peels a leading equipment part off a hyphen core, and never treats a previous `strength-band` token as absorbable.

Reproduced:
- `strength band-pull-apart` / `strength bar-muscle-up` / `strength ring-muscle-ups` / `strength cable-pull-through` → `{'strength'}`
- `strength-band pull-apart` / `strength-bands pull-apart` / `strength-band muscle-up` → `{'strength'}`
- Also brittle on whitespace: `strength  band pull-apart` / `strength\tband pull-apart` → `{'strength'}` (separator must be exactly one ASCII space)
- Twins clean: `strength band pull-apart`, `strength-band-pull-apart`

Share one modifier predicate with the hyphen path (or peel equipment from the head of a hyphen core before the strength-before-equipment check), and accept flexible whitespace between tokens the same way multi-word lexicon terms already use `[\s-]+`.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:147` — Round-7 widened the space-path separator check to `str.isspace()`, so modifier absorption now spans newlines/CRLF/blank paragraphs, not just horizontal runs.

```python
text[tokens[k].end() : start].isspace()  # True for \n, \r\n, blank lines
```

The commit claimed tabs/double spaces; `.isspace()` also treats vertical whitespace as “immediately preceding,” so a goal-vocab `strength` on one line is swallowed into a name core on the next.

Reproduced:
- `Objetivo: strength\nband-pull-apart 3x10` → clean (should flag `strength`)
- `Tu objetivo es strength\nband pull-apart` → clean
- `para ganar strength\n\nbar-muscle-up` → clean
- Contrast: `strength\n\nHaz band-pull-apart` still flags (intervening word)
- Contrast: `strength. band pull-apart` still flags (punctuation)

Restrict separators to horizontal whitespace only (e.g. `re.fullmatch(r"[^\S\n\r]+", gap)` or equivalent), so phrase-local absorb cannot cross line/paragraph boundaries.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:123` — `_absorbable` only accepts glued `strength-` + one equipment part, so multi-part glued modifiers before a core still false-flag `{strength}`.

Round-7 shared `_is_equipment` but left multi-part prefixes dual-coded: hyphen path uses `_is_allowed_prefix` (unlimited equipment/variant chain); space path only checks `startswith("strength-") and _is_equipment(second_part)`.

Reproduced:
- `strength-band-bar pull-apart` → `{'strength'}`
- `strength-band-cable pull-through` → `{'strength'}`
- `strength-bands-bar pull-apart` → `{'strength'}`
- Contrast fully hyphenated twins: `strength-band-bar-pull-apart` → clean
- Two-part `strength-band pull-apart` is clean

For multi-part tokens, reuse `_is_allowed_prefix(word.split("-"))` (keeping bare `strength` + peel of `following` for the space-separated case) so multi-part glued modifiers match the hyphen path.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:135` — `_HORIZONTAL_GAP_RE` is not true horizontal-only whitespace: it still matches vertical tab, form feed, and Unicode line/paragraph separators.

```python
_HORIZONTAL_GAP_RE = re.compile(r"[^\S\n\r]+")  # whitespace minus \n/\r only
```

Round-8 correctly flags `\n`/`\r` twins, but Python still fullmatches `\v`, `\f`, `\u2028`, `\u2029` (and `\x85`). Those gaps still let a preceding lexicon token be absorbed into the following name core.

Reproduced:
- `strength\u2028band-pull-apart` → clean (should flag `strength`)
- `strength\u2029bar-muscle-up` → clean
- `strength\vband pull-apart` / `strength\fband-pull-apart` → clean
- Contrast: `strength\nband-pull-apart` → `{'strength'}`

Tighten the class to horizontal ASCII only (e.g. `r"[ \t]+"` or an explicit allowlist of space/tab), matching the commit’s “tabs and double spaces” intent.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:152` — Space-path walk still hard-caps `absorbed < 2` while the hyphen path accepts arbitrary-length allowed prefixes, so the same name flags or cleans depending on separators.

After round-8 unified `_absorbable` onto `_is_allowed_prefix`, the leftover cardinality cap still stops the space walk after two tokens.

Reproduced:
- `strength-band-bar pull-apart` / `strength-band-bar-pull-apart` → clean
- `strength band bar pull-apart` → `{'strength'}` (only `bar`+`band` absorbed)
- Same for `strength bands bar pull-apart`, `strength cable bar pull-through`

Drop the magic cap and let `_absorbable` alone bound the walk — the predicate already stops on non-modifiers, so the cap is not required to keep `strength Muscle-up` / `muscle band pull-apart` flagged.

- pi code-review

[P1] `tests/behavioral/language.py:93` — `strength` is treated as name-internal anywhere it sits immediately before equipment in a modifier chain, so goal-vocab `strength` is laundered inside multi-part names (space and hyphen paths).

`_is_allowed_prefix` / `_absorbable` allow `strength` before any equipment part at any index, not only as a leading `strength band` unit. The unbounded left walk then covers it.

Reproduced (all return empty / miss `strength`):
- `kipping strength band pull-apart`
- `bar strength band pull-apart` / `band strength band pull-apart`
- `band-strength-band-pull-apart`
- `strength band strength band pull-apart`
- `stamina strength band pull-apart` → only `{'stamina'}`

Intended clean cases still work (`strength band pull-apart`, `strength-band-pull-apart`). Restrict `strength` to the first prefix part (or only as a single leading `strength`+equipment unit), so mid-chain / repeated `strength` flags as goal vocab.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/test_judge.py` — `language_consistency` weight 0.2 is not uniquely pinned: tone and language can trade weight while both overall worked examples stay green.

From `sum(w)=1`, `5t+5s+1n+5l=4.4`, and `5t+2s+5n+5l=3.95`: `n=0.15` and `s=0.35` are fixed, but `t+l=0.5` is free. e.g. `language=0.05` + `tone=0.45` still satisfies every numeric overall assertion and per-dimension gate.

Failure: language weight silently drops; overall/reporting underrates language misses while CI stays green. Pin `language_consistency` (and preferably each dimension) to its exact weight, not only the two overall scores.

- pi code-review

[P1] `tests/behavioral/language.py:159` — Space-path `first_in_run` treats any prior letter-token as mid-chain, so legitimate mid-prose `strength`+equipment names false-positive as strength leaks.

Round-10 correctly flags mid-chain `strength` inside a name (`kipping strength band…`), but `first_in_run` is true only when `k==0` or the previous gap is not horizontal whitespace. Any Spanish word before a real name fails that check, so the space form the tests carve out is unusable in chat.

Reproduced:
- `Hoy toca strength band pull-apart 3x10` → `{'strength'}`
- `vamos a hacer strength bands pull-apart` / `haz strength band pull-apart` → `{'strength'}`
- Contrast clean: bare `strength band pull-apart`, trailing `strength band pull-apart hoy`, parenthetical `(strength band pull-apart)`
- Contrast clean hyphen twins: `Hoy toca strength-band-pull-apart` / `Hoy toca strength-band pull-apart`

Restrict “not first” to when the previous token is itself an absorbable name prefix (equipment/variant), not any prior word in the sentence.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:164` — Glued `strength-band` tokens bypass `first_in_run` via `_absorbable`/`_is_allowed_prefix` (`strength` at local `i==0`), laundering mid-chain strength that the bare and full-hyphen paths both catch.

Reproduced:
- `kipping strength-band pull-apart` / `weighted strength-band pull-apart` → clean
- Contrast: `kipping strength band pull-apart` → `{'strength'}`
- Contrast: `kipping-strength-band-pull-apart` → `{'strength'}`

When absorbing a multi-part token that starts with `strength`, apply the same “first prefix of the whole name run” rule (reject if a prior absorbable token already sits to the left), so mixed glued forms match the bare/full-hyphen twins.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:20` — Lexicon omits `hypertrophy`, a primary DEFAULT_RULES_DOC goal with Spanish `hipertrofia` — same intake leak class as #67 is uncaught.

`ENGLISH_TRAINING_VOCAB` has `strength` / `endurance` / `muscle` but not `hypertrophy`. The shipped rules doc line is “General/hypertrophy goal (hipertrofia / masa muscular)”.

Reproduced: `¿Quieres ganar fuerza, hypertrophy, perder grasa…?` → `find_english_leaks` returns empty; bare `endurance`/`strength` would flag. Add `hypertrophy` (and any other DEFAULT_RULES_DOC English goal terms still missing) to the lexicon.

- pi code-review

[P1] `tests/behavioral/language.py:184` — Spaced modifier/lexicon before a fully glued `strength-band-{core}` token launders mid-chain `strength` — the round-11 discriminator never runs when `strength` is inside the core token itself.

`_is_name_core` accepts `strength-band-pull-apart` as one token; walk-back then absorbs `kipping`/`weighted`/`bar` without the strength mid-chain check (that check only runs when the absorbed token itself leads with `strength`). The shape matrix joins a prefix onto `unit='chain'` with `-`, never ` `, so CI misses it.

Reproduced:
- `kipping strength-band-pull-apart` / `weighted strength-band-pull-apart` / `bar strength-band-pull-apart` → clean
- `stamina strength-band-pull-apart` → only `{'stamina'}`
- Contrast twins flag: `kipping strength-band pull-apart`, `kipping-strength-band-pull-apart`, `kipping strength band pull-apart`

When a name-core token itself contains a `strength`+equipment prefix, treat left-side absorbable tokens as mid-chain the same way the bare/glued-split paths do.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:151` — `_preceded_by_chain_content` / `_is_lexicon` only inspect the single previous token via fullmatch, so multi-word and hyphen-compounded goal vocab do not mark following `strength` as mid-chain.

Reproduced:
- `weight loss strength band pull-apart` → only `{'weight loss'}` (strength absorbed as a fresh chain start)
- `fat loss strength-band-pull-apart` → fat/fat loss but not strength
- `stamina-endurance strength band pull-apart` → `{stamina, endurance}` without strength
- Contrast: unigram `stamina strength band pull-apart` and hyphenated `weight-loss strength band pull-apart` correctly include strength (previous token fullmatches)

Look back across a short horizontal run for any lexicon hit (or hyphen-split parts), not only `fullmatch` on the immediate previous token, before allowing `strength` to open a name chain.

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:208` — `preceded_by_lexicon` only fires when a lexicon hit ends exactly at the previous token's end, so goal-vocab hyphen compounds where the lexicon part is a proper prefix leave a following strength-led name uncut.

Round-12 fixed end-aligned forms (`weight loss`, `stamina-endurance`, `weight-loss`) but not prefix-shaped compounds: a hit on `muscle` inside `muscle-gain` ends mid-token, so `strength` at parts idx 0 stays name-internal.

Reproduced (strength missing / laundered):
- `muscle-gain strength band pull-apart` → `{'muscle'}`
- `stamina-focused strength-band-pull-apart` → `{'stamina'}`
- `lean-out strength band pull-apart` / `bulking-up strength band pull-apart` / `muscle-building strength band pull-apart`
- `weight loss-plan strength band pull-apart` / `fat loss-goal strength-band-pull-apart`
- Contrast still flags strength: `stamina strength-band-pull-apart`, `weight-loss strength band pull-apart`, `lean-muscle strength band pull-apart`

Treat a previous token as lexicon-preceded when any lexicon hit starts at the token start (prefix), not only when a hit ends at the token end.

- pi code-review

[P1] `tests/behavioral/language.py:211` — Overlap-based `preceded_by_lexicon` treats name-internal lexicon hits (`muscle` in `muscle-up`) as goal vocabulary, so a following strength-led exercise name falsely flags `strength`.

Round-13 widened the check from exact end-alignment to any overlapping lexicon hit. A hit on `muscle` at offsets (0,6) overlaps the `muscle-up` token (0,9), so `strength band pull-apart` is cut as mid-chain. `chin-up`/`pull-up` stay clean because they share no lexicon prefix.

Reproduced false positives (should be clean catalog pair):
- `muscle-up strength band pull-apart` → `{'strength'}`
- `bar-muscle-up` / `kipping-muscle-up` / `weighted-muscle-up` / `muscle-ups` + same chain → `{'strength'}`
- Contrast clean: `chin-up strength band pull-apart` / `pull-up strength band pull-apart`
- Contrast still correctly flags: `muscle-gain strength band pull-apart` → `{muscle, strength}`

Ignore lexicon hits that sit entirely inside an exercise-name span (or require the hit to cover a full previous token / not be a proper prefix of an allowlisted core).

- pi code-review

[P2] `tests/behavioral/language.py:49` — Multi-word lexicon separator class is ASCII hyphen/whitespace only, so typographic dashes miss `weight loss` entirely and also launder a following strength-led catalog name.

`_compile` joins parts with `[\s-]+` only. ASCII `weight-loss` still flags; U+2013/U+2014 variants do not.

Reproduced:
- `weight–loss` / `weight—loss` → empty
- `weight–loss strength band pull-apart` → empty (both the goal phrase and mid-chain strength stay clean)
- Contrast: ASCII `weight loss` / `weight-loss strength band pull-apart` still flag both terms

Normalize common unicode dashes to ASCII `-` before matching (and ideally before name-core tokenization, which has the same ASCII-only hole on `Muscle–up` / `strength–band–pull–apart`).

- pi code-review

[P1] `tests/behavioral/language.py:58` — Typographic en/em dashes split tokens while ASCII hyphens join them, so a dashed prefix before leading `strength` makes `strength` look chain-initial and fully false-cleans it.

Round-14 added en/em only to multi-word `_compile`; `_TOKEN_RE` still binds ASCII `-` only (`[letters]+(?:-[letters]+)*`). The dash becomes a token break: prev=`non`/`super` (prose) and `strength` starts a legal equipment name chain.

Reproduced:
- `non-strength band pull-apart` / `super-strength band pull-apart` → `{'strength'}`
- `non–strength band pull-apart` / `super–strength band pull-apart` (U+2013/U+2014) → empty
- Same gap partially misses strength after dashed goal compounds: `muscle-gain strength band pull-apart` → `{muscle, strength}`, but `muscle–gain strength band pull-apart` → `{muscle}` only
- U+2010/U+2011 still fully escape: `weight‐loss` / `weight‑loss strength band pull-apart` → empty (en-dash `weight–loss` flags)
